en: Catalogue of the Tripitaka Commentaries, Treatises, and Biographies, etc.,
totaling one hundred and thirty lacquer cases and two hundred and one fascicles, brought from Tang China for the study of the Dharma in the fifth year of the Kenpō era of the Kingdom of Japan;
including mandalas, mudrās, altar designs, portraits of various holy beings, śarīra relics, and other items.
*The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Great Auspicious Goddess, Free from Defilement*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Heart-Essence of All Buddhas*, one fascicle; *A Brief Account of the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions from the Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra*;
*The Sūtra of the Kharoṣṭhī Rishi*, one fascicle; *The Essential Collection of Dhāraṇīs*, one fascicle; and *The Request of the Youth Somahu*.
One fascicle of the Sūtra; one fascicle of the newly translated *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajña;
one fascicle of the *Ālidu-junduli-huguo-da-zizai-bazhele-mohe-butuo-jinshen-shenli-dharani*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ajita Rizi; and the *Vajraśekhara-padma-kula-hṛdaya-mantra*.
*Recitation Ritual* (2 fascicles); *Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Ritual for the Recitation of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel* (1 fascicle), translated by Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery.
The above nine works, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*The Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes according to the Vajraśekhara Yoga*, one fascicle;
*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Yoga of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and Vajrasattva*, one fascicle;
translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple; *The Recitation and Practice of the Five Secrets of Vajrasattva according to the Vajraśekhara Yoga*.
*The Ritual Manual for Recitation*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Mahāsukha-Vajrasattva, Extracted from the Vajraśekhara-sūtra of the First Yoga*, one fascicle;
*The Essential Yoga Method of Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa Bodhisattva*, one fascicle;
*Annotated Meaning of the Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by Vajrabodhi. *Vajraśekhara*... [text continues].
One fascicle: The Ritual for the Recitation of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes (Yogacārya-sahasrabhuja-sahasranetra-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-japa-vidhi).

One fascicle: The Ritual for the Bodhisattva Patadharāvalokiteśvara. One fascicle: The Separate Practice of Mudrās Extracted from the Section on Consecration in the Chapter on the Myriad Practices of All Bodhisattvas of the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa. One fascicle: The Ritual for the Recitation and Offerings of Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
The above ten works, totaling ten fascicles, were translated by Amoghavajra and are contained in the same volume.
*The Essential Ritual for the Four-Times Liturgy and Offering for Cultivating Mantra-Samādhi*, one fascicle;
*The Guide to the Eighteen Assemblies of the Vajraśekhara Yoga*, one fascicle; Translated by Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple: *The Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*.
*The Commentary on the Meaning of the Nī* (one fascicle), translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery;
*The Text for the Confession of Precepts according to the Instruction of the Supreme Vehicle* (one fascicle), translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery;
*The Mantra of the Great Original Aṭavaka for the Descent of Boundless Ambrosia and the Subjugation of All Ghosts and Spirits* (one fascicle); and the *Fire Altar Offering and...*.
*The Method for Nourishing the Ten Days*, one fascicle; *The Dhāraṇī Method for Bestowing Food upon All Emaciated-Faced Hungry Ghosts*, one fascicle;
*The Commentary on the Principle of the Prajñāpāramitā in the Mahāsukha-vajra-amogha-tattva-samaya Sūtra*, one fascicle.
The above eight works, totaling eight fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
One fascicle of the *Mahāvairocana Sūtra*, Chapter on the Wheel of Syllables, in Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
two fascicles of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* in Sanskrit and Chinese characters; one fascicle of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* in Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
one fascicle of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya Sūtra* in Sanskrit and Chinese characters; and [one fascicle of] the *Paramavimalaviśuddhaprabhā*.
*Mahādhāraṇī*, one fascicle; *Amoghapāśa-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle;
*Mahākāruṇika-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle; *Sarvabuddha-hṛdaya-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle;
*Sarvabuddha-hṛdaya-hṛdaya-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle.
One fascicle of the *Abhiṣeka Heart-to-Heart Mantra* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters); one fascicle of the *Dhāraṇī for Establishing the Boundary* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters);
one fascicle of the *Secret Heart Mantra* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters); one fascicle of the *Secret Heart-to-Heart Mantra* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters);
one fascicle of the *Praise of Samantabhadra’s Vows and Practices* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters); [and] the *Mahābuddha...* [title fragment].
*The Root Praise of the Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle; *The Combined Praise of the Great Buddha-uṣṇīṣa* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle;

*The Combined Praise of the Great Heart of the Dhāraṇī* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle; *The Praise of the Eight Classes of Devas and Nāgas* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle;
*The Praise of the Hundred-Syllable Mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle; *The Praise for Sending the Honored One Back to His Native Land*, one fascicle.
One fascicle: Praise of Maitreya Bodhisattva in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters; one fascicle: Praise of Maitreya (Maitrīputra) Bodhisattva in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters;
one fascicle: Praise of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters;
one fascicle: Praise of Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters; one fascicle: Praise of Vajragarbha Bodhisattva in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters.
One fascicle of the *Praise to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters; one fascicle of the *Praise to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;

one fascicle of the *Praise to Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin Bodhisattva* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters; one fascicle of the *Praise to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
one fascicle of the *Praise to Pūrṇapraṇidhāna* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters; [one fascicle of the *Praise to Vipaśyin* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters...]
One fascicle of the *Vairocana Buddha’s Miraculous Transformation and Empowerment: Auspicious Gāthās of Praise*, with both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
one fascicle of the *Maitreya Bodhisattva’s Compassionate Vow Praise after the Parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni Tathāgata*, with both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;

one fascicle of the *Verses on the Diamond Sūtra Treatise*, with both Sanskrit and Chinese characters; and the titles of the twenty-eight chapters of the *Lotus Sūtra*, accompanied by both Sanskrit and Chinese characters.
The *Names of the Arhats*, one fascicle; the above thirty-six works in thirty-seven fascicles are contained in the same volume.

The *Record of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, five fascicles, one volume, compiled by Wen Gong of Wuliangyi Temple; the *Collected Explanations of the Vimalakīrti* and the *Commentary on the Vimalakīrti from Guanzhong*, four fascicles, compiled by Daoyi of Zizheng Temple; and the *Explanation of the Subtle Points of the Guanzhong Commentary on the Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, two fascicles, composed by the Śramaṇa Qizhen of Mount Zhongtiao; the above two works totaling six fascicles are contained in the same volume.

*Fahua jing xiaowen lueshu* (A Brief Commentary on the Explanatory Text of the Lotus Sutra), three fascicles, one set; compiled by Shi Yanshou of Tiantang Temple. *Zhao lun lueshu* (A Brief Commentary on the Treatise of Sengzhao), one fascicle; composed by Jiu of Dongshan. *Zhao lun chao* (An Abstract of the Treatise of Sengzhao), three fascicles; compiled by Huizheng of Youxi Temple at Mount Niutou. *Zhao lun wenju tu* (A Diagram of the Phrases and Sentences of the Treatise of Sengzhao), one fascicle; compiled by Huizheng. *Zhao lun luechu yao yi jian zhu fu yan* (The Essential Meanings Extracted from the Treatise of Sengzhao, with Notes and Preface), one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Lingxing. The above four works, totaling six fascicles, are contained in the same set.

*Yinming niuchao* (A Mixed Compilation on the Science of Reasoning), three fascicles, composed by Zhe-lin of Zhangjing Temple; *Yinming yi-duan* (Decisions on the Meaning of the Science of Reasoning), one fascicle, composed by the Bhikṣu Zhao of Dayun Monastery; and *Yinming ruzhengli yizuan-yao* (Essential Compendium of the Meaning of Entering the Logic of Righteousness), one fascicle, compiled by [Name Lost] of Dashenlong Temple. These three works, totaling five fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Jiezhang song* (Verses on the Kalpa Chapters), one fascicle; *Jiezhang song shu* (Commentary on the Verses on the Kalpa Chapters), one fascicle, compiled by the Śramaṇa Bianzhi of Censhan; *Jiezhang song ji* (Record of the Verses on the Kalpa Chapters), one fascicle, composed by the Śramaṇa Daoquan; *Jiezhang kewen* (Outline of the Kalpa Chapters), one fascicle. The above four works, totaling four fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Great Master Zhizhe’s Cultivation of Samādhi: The Constant Practice Method*, one fascicle; *The Five Expedient Means: The Gate of Buddha-Recollection*, one fascicle; *Record of the Oral Instructions for Contemplating the Mind and Roaming the Mind* by the Great Master Zhizhe, one fascicle; *Explanation of the Meaning of the Forty-Two Characters* by the Great Master Zhizhe, one fascicle; *Mirror for the Buddhist Community* composed by Dharma Master Si of Mount Nanyue, five fascicles; *Compilation of the Meaning of the Twelve Divisions of the Sūtras through Mind-Contemplation* by the Monk Huixiang, one fascicle; *Outline of the Sūtras, Śāstras, and Commentaries Authored by the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai* recorded by [Tiantai] Ding, one fascicle; *Treatise on the Non-extinction of Body and Spirit*, one fascicle; and *Instructions for the Cultivation and Realization of the Lotus Samādhi* compiled by the Śramaṇa Haiyun of Lingxi, one fascicle. The above nine works, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in this single volume.
*The Dharma Master Kumārajīva’s Compendium on the Meaning of the Four *Siddhāntas* in Accordance with the *Sūtras*, One Scroll;

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra: The Gate of Not Falling into Negligence and the Twenty-nine Dharma Gates*, One Scroll; *The Ritual for Measuring Space and Weighing Lightness and Heaviness*, One Scroll;
*The Collected Karmavācanā Texts by Daoxuan*, One Scroll; *The Abridged Karmavācanā*, One Scroll; [Compiled at] Xida Yuan Temple by Huai.

*Suozhuanshuozui yaoxingfa* (Essential Methods for Confessing Sins), one fascicle, compiled by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing; *Zhuti diyu shouliang fenhuan* (The Lifespans and Limits of the Various Heavens and Hells), one fascicle, compiled by Zongrui of Zhongnan Mountain;

*Shou pusa jie wen* (Text on Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts), one fascicle; *Zuishangsheng foxing ge* (Song of the Buddha-nature of the Supreme Vehicle), one fascicle, composed by the Śramaṇa Zhenjue;
*Dacheng lengqia zhengzong* (The Orthodox Lineage of the Mahāyāna Laṅkāvatāra), one fascicle, [compiled by] the Sui dynasty [monk] from Lu[shan].

One fascicle of *Shan Yiai Si Huizhen Nianfo Sanmei Zhigui* (The Essential Guide to the Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation by Huizhen of Mount Yiai); one fascicle of *Fan Yu Za Ming* (Miscellaneous Sanskrit Terms);

and one fascicle of *Sijiao Shi Bing Daxiao Cheng Jie jue* (The Fourfold Regulations and the Precepts of the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna). The above thirteen works, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Biographies of the Dharma Gate of Master Nanyue Huisi*, two fascicles, compiled by Du Fei, Vice Director of the Imperial Guard; *The Letter from the Great Master of Tiantai to Emperor Wen of the Chen Dynasty*, one fascicle; *A Brief Record of Tiantai*, one fascicle; *The Praise for the "Chopping Pine" of Master Zhiyi*, one fascicle; *The Record of the Twelve Sites of the Way of Master Zhizhe of Tiantai*, composed by Ding, one fascicle; *The Biographies of Miraculous Manifestations of the Lotus Sutra*, composed by Ting, one fascicle; *The Biographies of Spiritual Resonance*, one fascicle; *A Brief Biography of Mount Qingliang*, one fascicle. These eight works, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Record of Baolin at Caoxi on Mount Shuangfeng in the Prefecture of Dazhou of the Great Tang*, ten fascicles, one set; preface by the Śramaṇa Lingche (style name Mingyong) of Kuaiji. *The Oral Transmission from Chan Master Zhi to Chan Master Yan of the Capital*, one fascicle; compiled by Niu Su of Dali together with the monk Zhiyan. *The Account of the Śramaṇa Wuxing of Nanjing Sent to the Kingdom of Tang from the Country of India*, one fascicle. *The Discourse on the Virtues of the Clergy and Laity by the Inner Palace Attendant Tanxian*, one fascicle, including the preface and text. *The Collection of New and Old Discourses on the Qi*, five fascicles. *The Response by Daguang Dharma Master of Yunhua Temple in the Capital to the Questions of the Crown Prince on the Definitive Meaning of Various Sutras, together with the correspondence*, one fascicle. *Discourses Praising the Virtues of the Clergy and Laity*, three fascicles. The above eight works, totaling twelve fascicles, are contained in this single set.

One scroll of the Stele for the Venerable Master Yan of Dong Dayun Temple in Yangzhou, with preface, composed by Li Yong; one scroll of the Stele for the Stupa of the Late Great Chan Master Dahe Shang Lengkaceṃ, with preface, composed by Lu Xun; one scroll of the Stele for Mount Gong of the Late Great Vinaya Master Śramaṇa Daoyuan, with preface, composed by Li Yong; one scroll of the Epitaph for the Great Dharma Master of the Translation Bureau at the Great Ci’en Monastery of the Great Tang, with preface; one scroll of the Stupa Inscription for the Great Dharma Master Ji of the Great Ci’en Monastery, with preface; one scroll of the Record of the Deeds of the Late Great Vinaya Master Daoxuan of Linggan Temple on Zhongnan Mountain; one scroll of the Eulogy for the Late Virtuous Daoxuan Vinaya Master of Ximing Monastery of the Great Tang; and one scroll of the Letter from the Great Master of Tiantai in Reply to Emperor Xuan of the Chen Dynasty. These nine works, totaling nine scrolls, are contained in this single fascicle.

*Newly Revised Ritual Manual for Auspicious and Inauspicious Occasions for Officials, Gentry, and Commoners of the Inner Clan of the Great Tang*, one fascicle; *Revised and Determined Kaiyuan Poetic Standards*, one fascicle, re-edited by Zheng Yuying; *Meanings of Official Responses*, one fascicle, composed by Xu Yin (style name: Suran); *One Hundred Judicial Judgments*, one fascicle, composed by Luo Binwang; *Collected Poems of Zhu Yuanying*, one fascicle; *Collected Poems Exchanged between Hangzhou and Yuezhou with Preface*, one fascicle; *Collected Poems*, five fascicles; *Seven-Character Verse Collection on the Twenty-eight Chapters of the Lotus Sutra*, one fascicle. The above twelve works, totaling forty-one fascicles, are contained in this single volume.
One set of five scrolls of the White-Drawn Great Maṇḍala of the Great Compassion Womb (Mahākaruṇā-garbha) of Mahāvairocana;
one set of seven volumes of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu; one scroll on the Seven Types of Altar Arrangements for Making Offerings to the Worthies and Sages;
one scroll on the Seventeen Altar Arrangements; and the seed-syllable maṇḍala patterns of the thirty-seven deities of the Vajradhātu.
One diagram of the seed-syllables (*bīja*) of the eighty-one deities of the Vajradhātu Maṇḍala; one diagram of the Lotus Sūtra Maṇḍala;
one diagram of the hand-seals (*mudrā*) of the Womb Realm (*Garbhadhātu*) Maṇḍala; one scroll of the Great Master Nanyue Huisi’s instructions on manifesting the skeletal shadow;
one set of three scrolls depicting the vision of the Aranya Bhikṣu seeing the shadow of Samantabhadra in the sky.
One image depicting Master Fahui reciting the Lotus Sutra before King Yama; one scroll depicting Master Shandeng’s experience of golden and silver palaces while reciting the Lotus Sutra;
one image depicting the divine beings who came to pay homage to Master Huibin while he was reciting the Lotus Sutra;
one image depicting the benevolent deities who came to listen to the sutra as Master Ying was reciting the Lotus Sutra; and [one image] of Master Ding.

A portrait of Tian Tong Jishi (Heavenly Youth Attendant) reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*; a record of Chan Master Huixiang’s posthumous birth of lotus flowers upon his grave and the constant sound of sūtras being recited from within it;
a scroll of the portrait of an old monk of Qin Commandery who instructed his disciples and manifested a dream to reveal his past causes;
and a record of Chan Master Daochao’s response to two successive lifetimes through his recitation of the *Lotus Sūtra*.
A portrait of the disciple’s birthplace; one portrait of Chan Master Fahui reciting the Lotus Sūtra, with light emanating from his mouth that illuminated the chamber;
one portrait of the Great Sage Śākyamuni; one scroll of the portrait of the Great Saint Mañjuśrī; five grains of śarīra;
two small glass vials containing the śarīra of three bodhisattvas; and a small white wax casket containing the śarīra of pratyekabuddhas—all of which were enshrined together.
The aforementioned Dharma-gate of the White Stone Vase and others.
Ennin arrived at the Great Capital of Yangzhou in the Tang Dynasty in the eighth month of the fifth year of the Jōwa era.
He traveled through the various temples within the city,
copying [the texts] as previously described.
Thereupon, the Venerable Zongrui of Zhongnan Mountain surpassed his predecessors in his learning.
He thoroughly investigated the profound subtleties and was able to interpret both Sanskrit and Chinese;
he was exquisitely proficient in the phonology of Siddham.
As he was departing for the Western Heaven (India) to bid farewell to his old acquaintances,
Wonren fortunately had the opportunity to pay him a visit and received instruction in the *Siddham* script of the Brahma Heaven.
He concurrently studied both Sanskrit and Chinese.
Furthermore, he encountered the Acharya Quan Ya, a disciple of the Acharya Xuanzang (Heng) who served as an Imperial Preceptor to the Great Tang,
from whom he received instruction in the secret teachings.
The Upādhyāya, moved by Dao-yuan’s sincerity,
entrusted him with the essential secrets;
he then instructed him in the dharma-gate of recitation.
He also brought the various mandala designs for both the Garbhadhātu and Vajradhātu families.
Subsequently, he intended to inquire about the Tiantai teachings;
however, because the journey was so vast and the time for his return would be lost, he did not go.
An imperial edict was issued forbidding my departure;
my regret and lamentation are beyond measure.
Although the Dharma-gates I seek have not yet been fully obtained, [I remain resolved].
Furthermore, the volumes have been recorded and verified as follows.
On the twentieth day of the fourth month in the year of Jiwu (the 4th year of the Kaicheng era of the Great Tang),
this was recorded by Ennin, a Dharma Master of the Transmission of the Lamp who was invited to seek instruction in the Tiantai school.
